newsitem.title: USA: U.S. machine tool demand $838 mln in October.
newsitem.headline: U.S. machine tool demand $838 mln in October.

text.p: U.S. demand for machine tools was estimated at $838 million in October, the American Machine Tool Distributors' Association and the Association for Manufacturing Technology said Sunday in a joint report.
Machine tool orders in September were $960 million, the two trade groups said a month ago.

Year-ago comparisons were not available. The latest figures were from the fifth U.S. Machine Tool Consumption report, which replaced monthly data on U.S. machine tool orders, shipments and exports that had been issued by the Association for Manufacturing Technology.

"Other than September, which reflected orders relating to IMTS (International Machine Tool Show), the nation's largest industrial trade show, October was the best month of the year," AMT President Albert Moore said in a statement.
"All sectors of the machine tool market continued to order new capital equipment as capacity utilization still remains over 80 percent," Moore added.
Machine tools are used to shape metal in making everything from bicycles to aircraft. Demand for these tools can provide a leading indicator of the pace of manufacturing.
The report said 3,517 machine tool units were ordered in October, down from 3,732 in September.

By region, the report said the Midwest accounted for 41.2 percent of national demand, followed by 21.6 percent in the Northeast. The Central region accounted for 14.5 percent of U.S. demand, the South 11.9 percent and the West 10.8 percent.
Export orders placed with U.S. builders totaled 289 units in October, down from 319 in September. In the first 10 months of this year, export orders were 2,592 units, the report said.
